findings.title: Response States beside the Written Judgment
findings.claim: Through 17:59's denied and wronged sign, Fātiha 1:7 adds two named recipient states, those angered and those astray, beside the focus's severe penalty. This supplies a differentiated response frame around the universal written town horizon without assigning a fate to either group.
findings.mechanism: The focus's عَذَابًا carries the penalty carrier; 17:59 supplies a specific local act of sign-denial and wronging; 1:7 names two different response states. Their contact lets the written communal horizon be viewed alongside a moral response taxonomy not named in Phase 1.
findings.reader_payoff: The town horizon can be held beside distinct response states while the local sign scene keeps the external link grounded.
findings.containment: Neither the people of 17:59 nor any town in 17:58 is identified with either 1:7 category, and the external verse does not assign destruction versus punishment. The overlay adds a response frame only.

epistemic.reason: The local denial/wronging contact is explicit in the supplied 17:59 text and trusted channel evidence. The two external response categories are explicit in 1:7, but their relation to particular communities or outcomes is not supplied.
